The 2d-NTMDI is a novel two-dimensional nonlinear tuned mass damper inerter.
The 2d-NTMDI consists of a mass and two sets of springs, dashpots, and inerters configured in two axes.
The 2d-NTMDI exhibits geometric nonlinearity due to the springs' configuration.
The 2d-NTMDI reduces bi-directional vibrations by converting linear motion to rotational motion.
The 2d-NTMDI can reduce bi-directional vibrations by 35%.
The 2d-NTMDI is applied to wind turbine blades to mitigate bi-directional vibrations and prolong fatigue life.
The 2d-NTMDI has the capability of reducing multi-mode vibrations.
The wind loading is calculated using the Blade Element Momentum (BEM) method.
The mean wind speed used in the study is 9 m/s.
The turbulent intensity used in the study is 15%.
The dimension of the mass matrix M˜ is 4x4.
The dimension of the stiffness matrix K˜ is 4x4.
The dimension of the damping matrix C˜ is 4x4.
The 2d-NTMDI has the potential to be used in other applications beyond wind turbine blades.
The 2d-NTMDI can be optimized using numerical search methods.
